item.author: Ling Xin
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin
item.description: Beijing has given the go-ahead for the Long March 9, a super heavy rocket often seen as China’s answer to SpaceX’s Starship, weeks after the American megarocket first reached orbit, according to a lecture slide circulating online. The stainless-steel giant received official approval last month, according to the slide. At 110 metres (361 feet) tall and 10.6 metres wide, it will be the most powerful and expensive launcher China has ever built. The slide, presented in the northwestern city of Xian...
item.title: Beijing approves giant Long March 9 rocket for deep-space and lunar base runs

item.author: Elizabeth Cheung,Fiona Sun,Eric Jiang
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Cheung,Fiona Sun,Eric Jiang
item.description: Hong Kong authorities have cracked down on a bid-rigging syndicate and arrested 28 people, including directors of contractors and consultancy firms as well as some with triad backgrounds, in the first operation by a joint task force after the devastating Wang Fuk Court fire. Secretary for Security Chris Tang Ping-keung said on Friday the task force, set up to combat bid-rigging, had also formed a 24-hour hotline for the public to report any suspected bid-rigging activities and would offer...
item.title: Hong Kong authorities arrest 28 in crackdown on bid-rigging after Tai Po fire

item.author: Ann Cao
item.dc:creator: Ann Cao
item.description: China’s pure-play artificial intelligence chipmakers crossed an important milestone in the third quarter as several firms swung into profit, but severe supply chain hurdles and soaring memory costs cloud their long-term growth prospects. Domestic graphics processing unit (GPU) developers including Moore Threads, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX are racing to fill the market void left by Nvidia, whose high-end processors face strict US export controls. These home-grown firms are competing fiercely to win...
item.title: China’s AI chipmakers report first profits, but will the trend continue?

item.author: Albee Zhang
item.dc:creator: Albee Zhang
item.description: Chinese state media showcased several Dongfeng-series missiles on Thursday to mark a key anniversary, including the nuclear-capable DF-61 intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) and the rarely seen DF-100 long-range supersonic cruise missile. The coverage coincided with social media reports suggesting that the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force might have conducted an inland ICBM test, potentially involving a ground-based mid-course missile interception, although neither activity has been...
item.title: China puts DF missiles on display as flight bans fuel speculation about ICBM test

item.author: Zoey Zhang
item.dc:creator: Zoey Zhang
item.description: Ahead of China’s Double 11 shopping spree, a viral WeChat mini-programme called “Wallet, Please Wait” is helping consumers curb impulse purchases. The free tool borrows from corporate finance workflows, outsourcing approval of everyday purchases to the crowd. Users can submit purchase requests detailing the item, its price, their reasons for wanting it and any cheaper alternatives. Shoppers can share requests with family members or post them to a public “plaza,” where purchases are approved or...
item.title: Viral Chinese app lets strangers vote on purchases to stop impulse buying

item.author: Kyodo
item.dc:creator: Kyodo
item.description: Japan’s government on Friday compiled a package of emergency measures to address a spate of recent personal data breaches caused by unauthorised access, amid growing public concerns over cybersecurity. Among the measures are promoting the use of artificial intelligence to identify vulnerabilities in computer systems and creating several teams of highly skilled experts. The package was announced at a meeting of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and relevant ministers on Friday. Takaichi instructed...
item.title: Japan deploys AI, specialist teams to counter cyberattack wave

item.author: Joseph Sipalan
item.dc:creator: Joseph Sipalan
item.description: Malaysia’s hope for a shift in US trade policy is unlikely to be realised for some time, experts warn, as the new Democratic-led Congress will face strong opposition from US President Donald Trump in its attempt to reverse some of his tariff measures. Trump’s Republicans suffered their worst rout in recent times in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, losing control of both Congress and the Senate by wide margins as voters made clear their anger at Trump over surging living costs caused by the...
item.title: Why Malaysia may still face trade uncertainty after US midterms

item.author: Cannix Yau
item.dc:creator: Cannix Yau
item.description: Temperatures in Hong Kong are expected to drop to as low as 18 degrees Celsius (64.4 Fahrenheit) on Tuesday as a cold front hits the city early next week. According to the Hong Kong Observatory, a strong monsoon over the weekend will bring cooler weather. “A strong northeast monsoon will affect the coast of Guangdong over the weekend. A cold front is expected to move across the coast of southern China at first on Monday,” the forecaster said on Friday. “Under the influence of the associated...
item.title: Hong Kong temperatures to fall to 18 degrees next week as cold front hits

item.author: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.dc:creator: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.description: Indonesia’s climate ambitions are being undermined by devastating wildfires that contradict its emissions-cutting strategy, casting a shadow over Jakarta’s push for a greener economy ahead of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (Cop31). However, Environment Minister Jumhur Hidayat has doubled down, arguing that his country’s climate goals should not come at the expense of national development and that emissions reduction efforts must be fair. On Wednesday, he outlined six priority areas for...
item.title: Indonesia doubles down on climate goals despite surging wildfire emissions

item.author: Alex Lo
item.dc:creator: Alex Lo
item.description: Comedian Patton Oswalt once joked about the United States electing a KKK president after the progressive years of Barack Obama. The joke is worth retelling, not just because it’s funny but because it captures the swing between extremes in US politics. That’s worth keeping in mind in light of the so-called Democratic blue wave sweeping the country. It goes: “We will have a woman president, probably sooner than later … but just keep in mind that after she serves her term, the choices will very...
item.title: Democrats’ blue wave means rough waters ahead for US-China relations

item.author: Holly Chik
item.dc:creator: Holly Chik
item.description: Chinese commercial space firm Light Year Explorer has manufactured a rocket fairing with a wooden outer skin as part of the company’s push for lower-cost, mass-produced launch vehicles. The design of the protective shell uses low-density plywood formed into a smooth aerodynamic curve, supported by an internal metal framework to bear loads, according to the Jiangsu-based company. “This configuration matches traditional composite fairings in key performance areas such as weight, structural...
item.title: Chinese space firm builds wooden rocket nose cone for cheaper, frequent launches

item.author: Aidan Jones
item.dc:creator: Aidan Jones
item.description: A former Miss Thailand and well-known social activist was arrested on Friday alongside her husband, accused of siphoning off money from her charity to buy luxury homes as police examine an estimated 1 billion baht (US$30 million) in donations. Panadda “Boom” Wongphudee, 50, was detained at her Bangkok home early on Friday morning after the Criminal Court issued arrest warrants accusing the couple of public fraud and money laundering. Her husband, fitness influencer and businessman Atip...
item.title: Ex-Miss Thailand arrested over claims charity donations funded luxury lifestyle

item.author: Sam Beltran
item.dc:creator: Sam Beltran
item.description: The Democratic Party’s sweep of both houses of the US Congress could stabilise Washington’s commitment to the Philippines, bringing relief to allies rattled by President Donald Trump’s Iran war and his shifting foreign policy. Analysts expect bipartisan support for Manila to endure, with Democratic oversight set to rein in Trump’s unpredictability. But they warn that Washington could still turn inward to deal with domestic challenges, diverting attention from the Indo-Pacific. The rebuke of...
item.title: Why Democratic Congress may enhance US-Philippines alliance, pivot to Asia

item.author: William Zheng
item.dc:creator: William Zheng
item.description: China’s top legislature has passed a landmark law targeting cross-border corruption, equipping Beijing with expansive new tools to pursue illicit offshore assets while countering foreign attempts to investigate wrongdoing in China. The Anti-Cross-Border Corruption Law was approved at the close of the 25th session of the 14th National People’s Congress Standing Committee on Friday and took effect immediately, according to state news agency Xinhua. The statute establishes formal mechanisms for...
item.title: The new anti-corruption law arming Beijing with wide global enforcement powers

item.author: Jim Au Yeung
item.dc:creator: Jim Au Yeung
item.description: An EU funding crunch is threatening to stifle the bloc’s ambitions to expand its influence in Southeast Asia, as Brussels grapples with a budget deadlock that could slow infrastructure investments across the fast-growing region. The funding squeeze could hinder the green transition and regional connectivity goals of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, even as Brussels seeks greater strategic autonomy amid competition with Beijing’s economic clout. Analysts expect the European Union to...
item.title: Is EU’s Southeast Asia push facing a funding crunch as China widens lead?

item.author: Gabriel Dominguez
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Dominguez
item.description: The US military has expanded its cybersecurity presence in Hawaii and set up a regional centre to better detect threats and disruptions to its Pacific communications networks. The new initiatives come amid US accusations of Chinese cyber operations targeting critical infrastructure, including on Guam, and concerns about the security of undersea cables linking the Pacific to the US mainland. Neither initiative has been explicitly linked to China. Brigadier General Michael Smith, US Pacific...
item.title: US military expands Pacific cyber hub to counter risks to undersea cable networks

item.author: Mia Nurmamat
item.dc:creator: Mia Nurmamat
item.description: The sweeping midterm election victory by US Democrats has triggered warnings from analysts that an impending regulatory clampdown could derail the nation’s multi-trillion-dollar artificial intelligence data centre buildout. Wall Street forecasters slashed their projections for Big Tech infrastructure spending hours after the vote, cautioning that a wave of proposed project moratoria and tighter oversight could stall up to 30 per cent of planned US facilities and force developers to downscale...
item.title: Does the Democratic midterm victory spell the end of US AI data centre boom?

item.author: Associated Press
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: Three people accused of using artificial intelligence to impersonate corporate executives and lawyers to steal about US$129 million have been indicted on charges of wire fraud and aggravated identity theft, prosecutors said Thursday. Over more than a year and a half, Jacob Soall, 41, Sharon Hazan, 54, and Guy Sheetrit, 42, targeted thousands of companies across the world in their AI scheme, according to the indictment filed in a US District Court in New York. Their victims included hospital...
item.title: US accuses trio of using AI to impersonate CEOs and lawyers to steal US$129 million

item.author: Zhu Wenqian,Enoch Yiu
item.dc:creator: Zhu Wenqian,Enoch Yiu
item.description: Hong Kong’s Exchange Fund, the war chest used to defend the local currency, reported a 74 per cent tumble in third-quarter earnings amid pervasive market uncertainty, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Friday. Earnings totalled HK$18.6 billion (US$2.4 billion) in the quarter, plunging from HK$70.8 billion a year earlier. For the first nine months of 2026, total earnings slid 39.6 per cent from a year earlier to HK$171.9 billion. The Exchange Fund’s Hong Kong equities portfolio...
item.title: Hong Kong’s Exchange Fund earnings tumble 74% as HKMA warns of more market turbulence

item.author: Fiona Chow
item.dc:creator: Fiona Chow
item.description: A Hong Kong court has sentenced a domestic helper to five months in jail for molesting her former employer’s 12-year-old daughter in the family home. Lady Jay Santos Flores, 45, offered no mitigation before she was sentenced at Kowloon City Court on Friday on three counts of indecent assault. She sobbed occasionally during the hearing. Flores was convicted last month of molesting the girl, who said the Filipino helper had touched her genitals on several occasions between May and June 2025. The...
item.title: 5 months’ jail for helper convicted of molesting employer’s 12-year-old daughter

item.author: Iman Muttaqin Yusof
item.dc:creator: Iman Muttaqin Yusof
item.description: Malaysia’s disgraced former prime minister Najib Razak moved closer to house arrest after Umno on Friday paid a 50 million ringgit (US$12.3 million) fine required under the terms of his royal pardon. The clemency granted by King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar in September allows Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 2028, after more than four years behind bars for corruption linked to the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund. Despite the payment, Najib has not been...
item.title: Malaysia’s Najib to remain in prison as legal questions linger despite fine payment

item.author: Emily Hung
item.dc:creator: Emily Hung
item.description: Hong Kong’s privacy watchdog has backed a proposed overhaul of rules to tighten access to land records, warning that journalists have no exemption when collecting data as complaints over information misuse appear to be worsening. Privacy Commissioner Ada Chung Lai-ling said on Friday that journalists do not enjoy an exemption under the Privacy Ordinance when gathering information, even though certain safeguards apply to how the data is subsequently used. “The Privacy Ordinance does provide an...
item.title: Hong Kong privacy watchdog backs tighter rules on access to land records

item.author: Tom Hussain
item.dc:creator: Tom Hussain
item.description: The close defence relationship between the United States and Israel is set to be restructured over the coming two years, with billions of dollars in direct annual military aid being phased out in favour of joint weapons technology programmes. US President Donald Trump shocked Israelis and Americans alike on Tuesday by suddenly announcing that the roughly US$4 billion a year in direct military funding Israel received from Washington would be cut off by the end of the year. item.author: Iman Muttaqin Yusof
item.dc:creator: Iman Muttaqin Yusof
item.description: Malaysia’s Sarawak will hold a state election on December 12 as the incumbent government seeks a fresh mandate to press demands over autonomy and control of the territory’s natural resources. The filing of nominations will begin on November 28 and early voting will be on December 8, Election Commission chairman Ramlan Harun told reporters on Friday. The 14-day election campaign involving more than 2.05 million eligible voters choosing 82 members will end on December 11, the commission said in a...
item.title: Malaysia’s Sarawak locks election date amid autonomy, resource control push

item.author: Finbarr Bermingham
item.dc:creator: Finbarr Bermingham
item.description: Weeks after the European Union and China struck a deal aimed at averting a looming trade war, the two sides remain at loggerheads over what is wrong with their relationship, how to fix it and who is to blame. At events in Brussels this week, threats were exchanged and differences rose to the surface. With the ink barely dry on their fragile trade peace, it was clear that both were still preparing for a trade war. “If the EU insists on adopting restrictive and discriminatory measures against...
item.title: EU-China truce under strain as both sides brace for potential trade war

item.author: Julian Ryall
item.dc:creator: Julian Ryall
item.description: Japan’s growing strategic partnership with Vietnam is putting Tokyo’s commitment to a rules-based regional order under scrutiny, as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces calls to press Hanoi over its failure to honour labour rights commitments. The issue is expected to surface during Vietnamese President To Lam’s four-day visit to Tokyo from Sunday, raising questions about how far Japan is prepared to defend the principles underpinning a major Pacific trade agreement when its economic and security...

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Canada unveiled a budget on Thursday that calls for “economic independence” and says that while reducing its reliance on the United States will take time, “the shift is under way”. Prime Minister Mark Carney’s second budget since taking office last year was presented to parliament just two days after President Donald Trump suffered a sweeping midterm election rebuke. While Democrats, who will take control of the US House and Senate next year, have already voiced a desire to ease Trump’s trade...
item.title: Canada budget charts ‘economic independence’ in decisive shift from US

item.author: Jess Ma,Matthew Cheng
item.dc:creator: Jess Ma,Matthew Cheng
item.description: Former Macau lawmaker Au Kam-san has been convicted on five out of seven charges in the city’s first national security trial, with the court handing him a 12½-year prison sentence. The Court of First Instance in Macau on Friday found the 69-year-old guilty on four counts under the city’s national security law – subversion of state power and establishing links with foreign groups or individuals to commit activities endangering national security – as well as a fifth count of violation of...
item.title: 12½ years’ jail for ex-Macau lawmaker Au Kam-san in city’s first national security trial

item.author: Khushboo Razdan
item.dc:creator: Khushboo Razdan
item.description: In the space of roughly 10 days, the two largest democracies in the Americas delivered setbacks to the populist right. In Brazil, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva staged a narrow but remarkable comeback, defeating Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, in a run-off election after trailing in the first round. This week, American voters handed control of both chambers of the US Congress to Democrats in a sharp rebuke of candidates riding on US President Donald Trump’s “Make America...
item.title: US and Brazil deliver double blow to the populist right. Will Europe feel the impact?

item.author: Alice Yan
item.dc:creator: Alice Yan
item.description: China’s first UFC champion recently shared that her family has been pressuring her to get married, but she is afraid to use her real name on dating websites for fear of revealing her identity. Thirty-six-year-old mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter Zhang Weili discussed her difficulties finding a boyfriend during an interview with mainland influencer Papi Jiang (known in English as Pepi Sauce) in late October. The interview has received a total of 230,000 likes and more than 10,000 comments across...

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Japanese and South Korean shares plunged on Friday after US shares tumbled overnight on worries that midterm election results could slow or derail the artificial intelligence data centre investment boom. Tokyo’s benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.1 per cent to 56,930 points in early trade. Seoul’s Kospi index dived 8.5 per cent to 4,923, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Investors had initially cheered Tuesday’s Democratic drubbing of US President Donald Trump’s...

item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday whom he will task with trying to form a new government, after the opposition’s Gadi Eisenkot secured a commanding number of recommendations to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Herzog held a second day of consultations with political parties on Thursday after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu - a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war - nor Eisenkot - a former military chief...
item.title: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tipped to seek Israeli government with backing of Arab lists

item.author: CNA
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.description: When Huang Baoying was growing up, her older brother helped look after her, their parents recalled. Huang Bocan would tutor his younger sister at night and help her with her studies, their mother said. To his parents, he was a responsible son whom they trusted to help care for Baoying while they worked long hours. Years later, he would be sentenced to life imprisonment for murdering her. “We never imagined that things could become so serious,” their father said after Bocan, 34, was sentenced on...

item.author: Julian Ryall
item.dc:creator: Julian Ryall
item.description: A month-long police campaign in Japan to track down hundreds of suspects sought over the nation’s most notorious crimes, some dating back decades, underscores what analysts describe as the surprising ease with which individuals can vanish, even in the country’s highly bureaucratic society. The nationwide drive, officially designated the “Month for Strengthening Investigations into Wanted Suspects”, began on November 1. Through official websites and social media appeals, authorities are urging...

item.dc:creator: Vasilis Trigkas
item.description: At their October meeting in South Korea last year, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, recognising mutual vulnerability to export restrictions, agreed to suspend some of the most draconian measures they had imposed on each other: US port fees on Chinese-built vessels and Chinese export controls on rare earths. item.dc:creator: Alcott Wei

item.author: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.dc:creator: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.description: South Korea’s government has announced it will revise a youth counselling manual that categorised homosexuality as a form of juvenile delinquency, after facing a backlash sparked by local media reports earlier this week. Published by the Korea Youth Counselling and Welfare Institute – a body affiliated with the Ministry of Gender Equality...

item.dc:creator: Associated Press

item.dc:creator: Eric Jiang
